text:
maria: Quick heads-up everyone — launching a 6-month pilot starting April 6 to expand short-term caregiver leave (STCL) and introduce an expedited travel reimbursement waiver for urgent family return trips. This is aimed at helping folks who need to travel on short notice for serious family caregiving needs. Details below and a short FAQ.

maria: TL;DR: 5 extra days of paid STCL (one-time allotment) + a travel waiver that speeds up reimbursement and allows retroactive approval in most emergency cases. Pilot applies to full-time employees, global eligibility depending on local law (see link). :sparkles:

maria: What changes:
• STCL: one-time +5 days paid caregiver leave, usable within 12 months, stacks with existing PTO but will be tracked separately.
• Travel waiver: covers economy airfare + reasonable urgent ancillary costs (one-way change fees, last-minute hotel up to 3 nights). Expedited processing target: 3 business days.
• Retroactive approval: up to 5 business days after travel if you submit documentation and emergency reason. We know emergencies aren’t scheduled.

aj: who exactly qualifies for "caregiving needs" here? parent/child/partner only or broader? :question:

maria: Good Q. Pilot covers immediate family (parent, child, spouse/partner), primary caregiver responsibilities (e.g., if you're the designated guardian), and in exceptional cases a dependent with medical need. If in doubt, ping people-ops and include a short note; we’ll lean supportive. Local labor laws may restrict some elements — local HR will confirm where needed.

devon: pay impact? is this paid at full salary or some percentage?

maria: It's paid at full base salary for the +5 days. If you’re on leave beyond that, standard leave policies apply. No changes to benefits accruals during STCL.

sam: Process question — do I need preapproval before booking travel? sometimes you book a flight immediately.

maria: We expect preapproval when possible but we built in the retroactive window for exactly those last-minute bookings. If you can, open a quick ticket in #people-ops with "STCL travel waiver" and the travel details; if not, submit receipts + brief note within 5 business days and mark it URGENT. We’ll triage and aim to reimburse within 3 business days. 

maria: Filing steps (short):
```1) Submit the STCL + travel waiver form: https://redwoodinference.internal/people-ops/stcl-waiver
2) Attach receipts and a one-line reason (e.g., "Urgent: flown home for parent surgery on 2026-04-03")
3) Select "Expedite" and tag payroll if reimbursement needed same-week
4) People Ops reviews; payroll processes reimbursements on expedited queue (3 business day goal)```

people-ops-bot: Updated policy doc uploaded: https://redwoodinference.internal/people-ops/policies/stcl-expedited-travel-2026.pdf — includes country exceptions and sample docs. :link:

linda: thank you — really appreciate this being easier. small ask: can we also have an obvious checkbox in the time-off flow for the +5 days so managers don't miss it?

maria: Great suggestion — we’ll loop in eng/devex to add a checkbox in the time-off form during the pilot. Filing an item with Product now. @devon i'll include you for manager guidance notes.

devon: happy to help with the manager quick-guide.

maria: FAQ quicks:
Q: Does this affect existing bereavement? A: No, bereavement policy remains separate.
Q: Can contractors use this? A: Not part of pilot; contractors should contact their manager and Finance for ad-hoc support.
Q: How long is the pilot? A: 6 months with a midpoint review after 3 months.

aj: any reporting/metrics we’ll share? curious if uptake will vary by region.

maria: Yes — we'll publish anonymized usage metrics (days used, reimbursements processed time) at the midpoint and final review. If you have concerns about privacy reach out.

linda: thanks again. passing to my manager for awareness.

maria: Thanks team — if you want to discuss edge cases DM me or drop in #people-ops. We’ll post an official all-hands blurb next week and update the handbook.
